Hundreds of people are pushing on this door. It won't open. How do you fix that for good?
Level one. Chicago, nineteen oh three.
Carl Prinzler sold door hardware. He was in Chicago the day the Iroquois Theatre burned.
The exits failed, and six hundred and two people died.
Carl couldn't let it go. You're Carl. Three options. Which one would you pick?
Unlock every exit before each show.
Put an usher at every exit, to open it.
Put a bar across the door. Push the bar, and the door opens.
Option A sounds obvious. But some of those doors opened inward. With a crowd pressed against it, even an unlocked door won't open.
Option B sounds safe. But the theatre had ushers. They had never had a fire drill, and some didn't know the exits.
Option C is what Carl built, with his neighbor, an architect. It took them five years. The crowd pushes the bar, and the door swings out.
Today, codes require it on the exits of theaters and schools that hold fifty people or more.
Level cleared. Comment what you picked, and follow for level two.
